inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-24T20:00:03Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 190.75-313.55
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% built on a US large-cap risk-free rate (~4.3% 10yr UST) plus an equity risk premium of ~5.5% levered to AJG's beta (~0.9-1.0, moderately cyclical fee-based brokerage with elevated post-deal leverage ~3.0x net debt/EBITDA); a touch below the house 9-10% US-tech default reflecting AJG's highly recurring, non-cyclical-relative-to-tech commission revenue base and investment-grade credit profile, but above a pure bond-like utility given P&C pricing-cycle and integration risk.
inputs.lease_treatment: Office leases are operating leases under ASC 842, immaterial relative to flows for a people/commission business (no owned real estate, no heavy plant); not separately modeled -- lease expense sits inside the EBITDA margin as a normal opex item, consistent with treatment A (expensed in EBITDA, no separate net-debt lease liability add-back).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest disclosed; consolidated net income is materially all attributable to AJG shareholders (Gallagher Bassett and international subsidiaries are wholly or near-wholly owned).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF component DCF per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing table (fee/commission-based insurance brokerage -- capital-light, no underwriting risk carried on AJG's own balance sheet, distinguishing it from the Residual-income-on-book model used for banks/deposit-takers and the BVPS-compounding model used for risk-carrying insurers like FRFHF/IAG.AX). AJG is confirmed NOT an underwriter: it earns commissions/fees for placing risk with third-party carriers (Brokerage, 89% of revenue) and third-party claims administration/consulting fees (Risk Management/Gallagher Bassett, 11%); it holds client premium in a fiduciary capacity (not its own balance-sheet risk) and its investing/financing cash flows are ordinary corporate finance, not underwriting reserves. FCF BASE NORMALIZATION: FY2025 reported OCF ($1,930M) and FCF ($1,785M, 12.8% margin) are depressed by one-off AssuredPartners transaction/integration costs and fiduciary-fund working-capital timing around the 2025-08-18 close (quarterly OCF swung from -$424M in Q2-2025 to +$753M implied in Q4-2025); TTM OCF through Q2-2026 recovered to $2,449M (computed as FY2025 $1,930M - H1-2025 $448M + H1-2026 $967M), confirming FY2025 understates the run-rate. Rather than carry the depressed FY2025 margin forward or the noisy TTM figure, the component build starts EBITDA margin at 27.5% (below AJG's own guided Brokerage-segment EBITDAC range of 33.6-34.2% to reflect Risk Management's lower-margin mix at 11% of revenue plus corporate costs) and ramps to 30% by Year 5 per management's guided +40-60bps/yr underlying margin expansion plus AssuredPartners synergy capture ($160M run-rate by end-2026, up to $325M by early 2028), producing an owner-FCF margin path of 22.2% (Year 1) rising to 24.0% (mature) -- comfortably inside AJG's actual FY2021-2022 pre-mega-deal FCF margins of 19-23%, so this is a normalization, not an aggressive assumption. D&A is set at 7.5% of revenue near-term (vs actual FY2025 D&A of $1,122M = 8.0% of revenue per XBRL DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet, and FY2026 guided intangible amortization of $1,105M per FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsAmortizationExpenseNextTwelveMonths), tapering to 6.0% by Year 10 as the AssuredPartners acquisition intangibles season and are only partially replaced by ongoing tuck-in amortization -- this D&A is genuinely non-cash (purchase-accounting intangible amortization, not maintenance capex) and is added back correctly in the owner-FCF build. HISTORICAL CAGR DIVERGENCE: Equity 3yr/5yr CAGR (36.4%/30.2%) is inflated by the ~$9.8B AssuredPartners-related equity raise, not organic book compounding; EPS CAGR (3.4%/6.4%) and owner-FCF-proxy CAGR (roughly flat to slightly negative over 2022-2025) are depressed by acquisition dilution, transaction costs and elevated D&A/interest expense from deal financing. None of the standard CAGRs is a clean organic-growth proxy for a company that just completed its largest-ever acquisition, so forward growth is anchored instead on management's own guidance (Brokerage organic ~5% for FY2026, cut from ~5.5% at the September 2026 investor update; Risk Management organic 9-12%, reaffirmed; blended total organic ~6%) plus AJG's decades-long tuck-in M&A algorithm (historically ~$1B+/year of smaller acquisitions on top of organic growth), moderating from a high-single-digit blended rate in Year 1-2 (reflecting the AssuredPartners full-year consolidation step plus continued tuck-ins) toward a long-run mid-single-digit organic-plus-modest-M&A rate, tapering to a 2.5% terminal growth rate. TAX: cash tax rate ramps from 19% (below AJG's ~21-23% GAAP effective rate, reflecting continued acquisition-related tax shields/interest deductibility in the near term) to a steady-state 21% (US federal statutory) by Year 5, consistent with interest expense on the AssuredPartners debt ($5.0B senior notes) providing a genuine, non-repeating near-term shield that fades as the debt amortizes/refinances. WORKING CAPITAL: set to 0% capture -- AJG's cash-flow swings are dominated by fiduciary-fund timing (client premiums held briefly before remittance to carriers), which is a balance-sheet/agency item that nets to roughly zero economically over a year and does not scale cleanly with revenue growth the way SaaS deferred revenue does; modeling a non-zero capture would risk mistaking fiduciary-fund noise for a genuine growth-linked tailwind or drag. HORIZON: 10 years, since the Year-5 owner-FCF margin (23.6%) is still short of the Year-10 mature margin (24.0%) and AssuredPartners synergy capture continues through early 2028.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (36.4%/30.2%) diverges massively (>30%) from Revenue (17.7%/14.8%), EPS (3.4%/6.4%) and FCF (-2.8%/3.2%) CAGRs. This is NOT organic value creation: AJG raised ~$9.8B of fresh equity in Dec 2024/Jan 2025 to fund the $13.8B AssuredPartners acquisition, mechanically inflating book value and shares outstanding (250M->257M) while transaction costs, step-up D&A and deal financing interest simultaneously depressed EPS and FCF. None of the standard historical CAGRs is used directly as the forward growth driver; see inputs.notes for the guidance-anchored approach used instead.

base.narrative: Base case: management delivers on its own (just-lowered) guidance -- ~5% Brokerage organic growth, 9-12% Risk Management organic growth, blended ~6% total organic for FY2026 -- while AssuredPartners integration proceeds roughly on the stated timeline ($160M synergies by end-2026, up to $325M by early 2028), and AJG continues its historical ~$1B+/year tuck-in M&A pace on top of organic growth. Property pricing softness (-10% renewal premiums in Q2 2026) is a genuine but partial offset, absorbed within the organic growth guide rather than derailing it, since casualty (+3%) and professional lines (+1%) remain firm. Margin expands 40-60bps/yr as guided plus synergy capture, reaching a mature ~30% adjusted EBITDA margin by Year 5-6 as Risk Management's lower-margin mix is diluted by scale in claims administration and shared-services leverage offsets corporate costs. Growth decelerates from a high-single-digit rate (AssuredPartners full-year consolidation effect plus tuck-ins) to a mid-single-digit long-run algorithm as the deal fully laps and the M&A pipeline normalizes.

bull.narrative: Bull case: AssuredPartners synergies are captured ahead of schedule and exceed the $325M ceiling as cross-sell between AJG's specialty practice groups and AssuredPartners' middle-market distribution outperforms, Gallagher Bassett sustains double-digit organic growth at the top of its 9-12% guided range, casualty/professional-lines pricing strength more than offsets property softness so total organic growth reaccelerates past the ~6% guide, and AJG continues sourcing well-priced tuck-ins at its historical pace without bidding the M&A market up. Operating leverage from shared global support centers compounds faster than guided, pushing adjusted EBITDA margin toward the low-33% area (still below Brokerage-segment-only guidance of 33.6-34.2%, appropriately blended down for Risk Management mix) as scale economies broaden.

bear.narrative: Bear case: the September 2026 guidance cut proves to be the leading edge of broader deceleration rather than a one-off Q4-timing adjustment -- property pricing softness spreads into casualty and professional lines as the broader P&C market turns, Brokerage organic growth settles near 3% rather than recovering toward the historical mid-single-digit algorithm, and AssuredPartners integration proves harder than guided (realized synergies land well below the $160M/$325M targets as historically seen with outsized brokerage mega-deals), keeping the adjusted EBITDA margin closer to 26-27% rather than reaching the guided maturity level. Elevated leverage (~3.0x net debt/EBITDA post-deal) constrains the pace of further tuck-in M&A, and higher-for-longer rates keep interest expense on the $5.0B AssuredPartners notes a persistent drag, holding the cash tax rate up via reduced interest-deduction benefit versus the base case. Growth still stays modestly positive throughout (a mature, largely non-discretionary commercial-insurance-adjacent revenue base with high renewal retention does not go into outright decline even in a soft cycle) so the terminal value is not zero-floored, but the compounding algorithm that has driven AJG's premium multiple visibly stalls.

scenario_narratives.base: Management delivers its own just-lowered guidance (~5% Brokerage organic, 9-12% Risk Management organic) while AssuredPartners integration proceeds on the stated synergy timeline and AJG resumes its historical tuck-in M&A pace; margin expands toward a ~30% mature adjusted EBITDA level via guided 40-60bps/yr underlying expansion plus synergy capture.
scenario_narratives.bull: AssuredPartners synergies beat the $325M ceiling and land early, Gallagher Bassett sustains the top of its double-digit organic range, casualty/professional-lines pricing strength offsets property softness so total organic growth reaccelerates, and disciplined tuck-in M&A continues at historical pace -- pushing the mature margin toward the low-33% area.
scenario_narratives.bear: The September 2026 guidance cut is the leading edge of a broader P&C pricing-cycle turn rather than a one-off Q4 timing fix; AssuredPartners integration underdelivers on its synergy targets as outsized brokerage mega-deals often do, elevated post-deal leverage constrains further tuck-in M&A, and the mature margin stalls in the mid-to-high-20s% rather than reaching 30%+ -- though the recurring, high-retention commission base keeps growth modestly positive throughout rather than going negative.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the house default 15% to 25% (and bull correspondingly trimmed to 25%) because AJG enters this valuation immediately after its largest-ever acquisition ($13.8B AssuredPartners, closed 2025-08-18) with net debt/EBITDA near 3.0x -- above its historical norm -- and has JUST cut its FY2026 Brokerage organic growth guidance (5.5% -> ~5%) alongside a wave of sell-side price-target reductions (RBC, Wells Fargo, KBW). This is a live, unresolved integration-execution risk (management itself removed a previously assumed Q4 2026 acceleration from guidance) layered on top of ordinary P&C pricing-cycle softness (property renewals -10% in Q2 2026), which is more than the generic 'growth disappoints' bear case the house default is calibrated for. Bull weight is trimmed symmetrically rather than base, since the base case already embeds management's own (already-lowered) guidance as the central estimate.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AJG is a capital-light, fee/commission-based global insurance brokerage (third/fourth-largest globally) with a decades-long algorithm of mid-single-digit organic growth plus continuous tuck-in M&A, now digesting its largest-ever acquisition (AssuredPartners, $13.8B, closed August 2025). The valuation is built on an owner-FCF component DCF anchored to management's own (recently trimmed) FY2026 guidance rather than historical CAGRs, which are badly distorted by the AssuredPartners equity raise and deal-related D&A/interest. Elevated D&A (~7.5%-8% of revenue, mostly purchase-accounting intangible amortization) is genuinely non-cash and is added back correctly in the FCF build; the near-term normalized EBITDA margin (27.5% ramping to 30%) sits meaningfully below AJG's own guided Brokerage-segment-only EBITDAC range (33.6-34.2%) to reflect the lower-margin Risk Management mix and corporate costs, which is a deliberately conservative blend. FY2025 reported FCF ($1,785M, 12.8% margin) is a trough distorted by acquisition-close transaction costs and fiduciary-fund working-capital timing -- TTM OCF through Q2-2026 recovered to $2,449M -- so the base FCF for the DCF is built from normalized components rather than carried forward from the depressed FY2025 actual.
key_risks_to_valuation: AssuredPartners integration execution -- the largest deal in company history; realizing $160M-$325M of targeted synergies carries meaningful execution risk, and management already removed an assumed Q4 2026 acceleration from guidance
Softening P&C pricing cycle (property renewals -10% in Q2 2026) could spread into casualty/professional lines, which have so far remained firm and are propping up the organic growth guide
Elevated leverage (~3.0x net debt/EBITDA) narrows financial flexibility for further tuck-in M&A and increases interest-expense sensitivity to rates
Premium valuation historically afforded to AJG (trailing P/E ~38-39x pre-cut) leaves little room for further guidance disappointments
Structural reliance on continuous, well-priced M&A to sustain the growth algorithm; a thinner or more expensive acquisition pipeline would compress the long-run growth assumption

D&A build is a modeling judgment (7.5% of revenue tapering to 6.0%) calibrated to disclosed intangible-amortization schedules but sensitive to the pace and size of future tuck-in acquisitions, which reset the amortization base each time
